The design itself says the preserving path may only run on already initialized pairs. title: NaN divergence between set_v truncation and generic conversion unstated
section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve (Conversions and numerical behavior)
claim: Omission: the design says the two conversions 'handle NaN differently' but does not state the rule, while its test row asks for independently chosen expected bits for NaN and infinity. The design's description of the set_v path (convert to fp32, keep the upper 16 bits) is confirmed correct. The exact divergence is this: for an fp32 input whose exponent field is all ones and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, set_v keeps the upper 16 bits unchanged, so a NaN whose upper 7 mantissa bits are zero becomes +/-Inf (0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80). fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic conversion in simd/bf16.hpp) first ORs 0x00010000 into such inputs, so the result is always a NaN (0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F81). Infinity, denormal and finite inputs convert identically in both paths (truncation, no rounding, no flush to zero). The fp16 path has the same property after cvtph_ps (fp16 0x7C01 becomes fp32 0x7F802000, then set_v gives 0x7F80 = +Inf and the generic path gives 0x7F81). In the 8-lane build the row-view .set() path uses fp32s_to_bf16s, so the two builds legitimately give different bits for those inputs, and the test's expected values must be chosen per build.

title: "Placement construction" wording admits std::construct_at, which zero-fills the arena
section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve - Storage and how long its objects remain valid
claim: Ambiguity: the design tells the implementer to use "placement construction" but not which form. std::construct_at(p) with no arguments is defined as ::new (p) T(), which is value-initialization. Value-initialization of a class whose default constructor is defaulted and not user-provided first zero-initializes the whole object. The design's own owner (vnni_tensor, the proposed V storage class) has exactly such a constructor, so std::construct_at, new (p) T(), and new (p) T{} would all write zeros over every KV block of a multi-GB arena at allocation and at restore. title: std::start_lifetime_as is not in the pinned toolchain; construction requirement should cite its basis

claim: Factual gap: the "supported C++23 function for starting object lifetimes" is std::start_lifetime_as (P2590R2). The repository pins Clang 19 (llvm19.stdenv) with GNU libstdc++ and -std=c++23. libstdc++ through GCC 15 and libc++ through LLVM 20 list P2590R2 as not implemented, so the option the design offers is not available (vendor status pages; the implementer should re-check in the pinned nix store, as the design already asks). title: Owner-is-an-expr left unstated; the rvalue-slice argument depends on it

claim: Ambiguity: the design never says whether vnni_tensor inherits expr<vnni_tensor, R, D> (tron's matrix expression base). The choice matters for three things the design relies on: whether tensor<64,128> t(owner) and dtensor(owner) compile directly, whether the general expression slice overload (which takes expr<B,d0,d1> const& and captures it by reference) can bind an rvalue owner at all, and therefore whether the design's sentence "Deleting only as_view() && is insufficient" is true (it is true only if the owner is an expr; otherwise the Owner& slice overload cannot bind an rvalue and the hazard does not exist).

title: Row chunk/set mechanics unspecified; existing primitives and the override signature should be named
section: 5. Interface design - operations table (matrix[token].chunk(i), bf16_chunk(i), row.set(expr))
claim: Ambiguity: the design requires vector extraction for chunk(i) and pair-preserving row.set(expr) but does not say how a chunk maps onto the packed pair or how the even/odd merge happens. The existing chunky<bf16,aligned>::set only handles contiguous rows, and the existing strided-view set path is scalar, so neither can be reused. The primitives already exist in the codebase: scaled_v_expr::even_part/odd_part turn one 64-byte pair load (32 bf16, 16 dims) into the fp32 chunk with one shift or one and, and page::set_v's odd path shows the merge (cvtepu16_epi32, slli 16, ternarylogic, store). The expr base detects a bf16_chunk override only by comparing member-function pointers, so vnni_row must declare a non-template `bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t) const noexcept` with that exact signature or the base silently falls back to fp32 conversion. A stride-2 rank-1 view (view<bf16,false,false,seq<D>,sseq<2>>) already represents the logical row correctly but with scalar chunk() and set(); the design should say this alternative exists and why a new row type is preferred.

recommendation: Add a short mechanics paragraph: chunk i of a packed row is one 64-byte load of 32 bf16 at pair_base + 32*i (64-byte aligned when the plane is); even rows use slli_epi32 16, odd rows use and 0xffff0000, then cast to fp32s (reuse even_part/odd_part); bf16_chunk narrows the selected half with cvtepi32_epi16; set expands the source bf16s to 32-bit lanes, shifts for odd, loads the pair, merges with ternarylogic or mask_blend_epi16 (0x55555555 / 0xAAAAAAAA), stores. Require the exact override signature for bf16_chunk. Add one sentence rejecting the stride-2 view alternative because its chunk()/set() are scalar.

title: Rvalue deletion must cover const&& and use all-or-none ref-qualification
section: 5. Interface design - operations table (owner.as_view())
claim: Omission: deleting an rvalue-qualified overload is legal and useful (a temporary owner's as_view() or operator[] fails at compile time), but C++ forbids mixing ref-qualified and unqualified overloads of the same name, so as_view() needs the full set: &, const&, && = delete, const&& = delete. Ben's straw-man and the design list only &, const& and && = delete; a const rvalue (for example a function returning const vnni_tensor by value) then binds to the const& overload and yields a view of a dead temporary. Ref-qualifiers are not special member functions, so they do not affect trivial copyability, and tensor's std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) constructs tensor<d1> rows, not the owner, so there is no interaction there.
evidence: C++23 [over.load]/2.3 (member functions with the same name and parameter-type-list cannot be overloaded if some but not all have a ref-qualifier); [class.prop]/1 (trivially copyable depends only on special member functions); facts.md Ben #3: "as_view() & / const& / && = delete"; h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:274@f46e48bab498 (`std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]);`).
design_quote: Delete overloads for rvalue owners (temporary values or objects marked for moving). [...] Apply the same restriction to owner indexing. Apply it to every function returning access to the owner's storage without a copy.
recommendation: Spell out the four overloads for as_view() and for operator[]: `&`, `const&`, `&& = delete`, `const&& = delete`, and note that all overloads of each name must carry a ref-qualifier.

title: matrix.set's no-read pair store cannot apply to slices starting or ending at an odd token
